Docs/Teleoperation

Teleoperation

Collect wrist and finger motion, then review and replay the resulting demonstrations.

Human motion to joint targets

The collection setup uses a Quest 3 headset, MANUS Meta Gloves Pro and controllers mounted on the backs of the hands. Wrist tracking drives arm inverse kinematics; calibrated finger retargeting drives the selected hand.

  1. Select a formal collection target and match its environment ID and robot UID in the control and mirror processes.
  2. Calibrate the selected hand’s tracking and retargeting profile.
  3. Check the launch configuration with the available --dry-run mode before starting collection.
  4. Review the pending episode/video, then validate state restoration and open-loop replay before release.

Ports and profiles

The Sharpa bridge uses upstream port 2044 and downstream port 6668. Wuji and XHand use their own configurations. Do not reuse a hand-specific SDK or joint map without checking the selected embodiment.

The canonical registry contains 40 formal targets: 10 long-horizon environments and 30 stages. Older launch notes can contain retired counts; task/config/collection_targets.py takes precedence.

Keep credentials out of shared artifacts

SDK credentials belong in the local runtime setup, not in website documentation, logs or dataset exports. The site intentionally does not publish raw SDK command files.

Address already in use

If the SDK reports a ZeroMQ bind error, inspect the owning listener before starting another copy:

ss -ltnp '( sport = :2044 or sport = :6668 )'

Reuse the running bridge or close its owning terminal cleanly. Do not kill unrelated processes or change just one end of a paired connection.
